title: Probing LLMs' Knowledge of Their Own Governance Documentation

novelty_assessment.label: mostly_novel
novelty_assessment.reasoning: LLM confabulation detection is well-studied (semantic entropy methods, probing hidden states), and LLM governance is a growing field. However, the specific experimental design of testing whether LLMs can accurately reproduce facts from their own company's governance documentation (safety policies, usage policies, model cards) versus confabulating plausible-sounding but incorrect details is novel. No published work systematically probes models' factual accuracy about their own governance constraints. 'Can LLMs Detect Their Confabulations?' (arXiv:2508.08139, 2025) studies general confabulation detection but not self-governance knowledge. The closest work is on LLM self-knowledge and calibration, but not applied to governance documentation specifically. This is a creative and accessible research design.
